tasks.short: See if this month and the next quarter still hold.

today.trigger: The week starts, or the management team asks whether the month will land.
steps: Open Power BI on yesterday's AFAS extract and export the three site results to Excel.
Add Rabobank cash and open items the nightly refresh has missed.
Ask the FP&A analysts which volume, fuel and flex figures they still doubt.
Write a short status for this month and the next quarter.
Defend or change that forecast with the management team.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same bridge because the extract and the ledger differ.
Chasing a flex invoice or a fuel posting that landed on the wrong site.
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes into making one version of the figures, and the forecast call comes last.

lenses.faster: The export and the Excel bridge, about half this task, disappear. What stays is about an hour and a half a week: reading the note, sending back a driver FP&A cannot support, and the forecast conversation with the management team.
lenses.autonomous: It starts Monday after the nightly AFAS extract, or when a driver crosses a threshold the director has set. The pack and the draft note run on their own. The gate is the director's approval before the management team or a site sees the note.
lenses.ambitious: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get one Monday page they can use before placing flex and overtime, which they do not get as a regular service today. Demand would grow if that page were cheap, because each site, and then each shift, would ask for its own cut, so the page stays one note with three site blocks.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the Excel bridge after every nightly refresh. The work worth keeping is the argument about whether next month's forecast is one the management team can be held to.
lenses.options: A reading that uses the site's volume, and a reading that uses FP&A's volume, change whether the management team cuts flex orders or holds them. Both readings sit on the same cash and margin lines.
lenses.altitude: Mondays start with a check of one note and a conversation about the drivers, and the workbook build leaves the week. The director gains the right to set which variances reach that note, keeps the right to issue the forecast, and becomes more expert on volume, fuel and flex at the three sites.
reach: The FP&A analyst's Monday variance note, once the director can trace volume, fuel and flex hours to the three site results.

tasks.human_edge: The management team will hold the director to the forecast. The director can tell a lost contract at one site from a slow month, and can reject a line that is not in the pack. Choosing which supplier to pay first, or whether to draw the Rabobank facility, stays with the director.
tasks.pattern_why: The figures already sit in AFAS, Power BI and the bank files, and the weekly steps are fixed. One model call turns that pack into a note where every figure names its source, which a person can check line by line.

in_practice.trigger: Every Monday at 07:00 after the nightly AFAS extract, or when volume, fuel or flex hours cross the threshold the director has set.
steps: A fixed job pulls cash from Rabobank CAMT.053 and AFAS open items, the three site results, DSO and the current FP&A forecast lines.
Supplier payments in the 13-week cash line use the terms stored in AFAS, with small suppliers inside 30 days where BW 6:119a(6) applies.
One model call writes a single note. Every figure is copied from a named AFAS account, the extract date, or a forecast line.
The note names at most three drivers for the next 13 weeks: volume, fuel and flex hours, at site level.
The director checks the note, strikes out any line that is not in the pack, and approves the reading the management team sees.
in_practice.human_gate: The management team and the site managers see only a note the director has approved. Any choice to pay one supplier ahead of another, or to draw the facility, is made in that same approval.
data_needed: Trial balance and open items by site
Flex hours and fuel at site level
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint finance-control library: extract date, sources, draft, edits, and the name and time of the approver.

evidence.claim: Among 336 Dutch finance professionals, 81% explain DSO after the fact, 12% plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead, and 75% of CFOs cannot explain an AI-driven decision. A status note has to show its workings.

Executive reporting takes about 32 hours a month, and 30% of the most AI-mature finance teams spend over 40 hours, against 17% of early-stage teams. Extra cuts can consume the time saved. Survey of 2,000 finance executives in the US, UK, France and Germany, with no Dutch slice.
Tax estimates, strategic purchases and cash allocation need a person's approval, with timestamped logs.
At Noordhaven this task is the company's own result and 13-week forecast across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, read from AFAS, Power BI and Rabobank.

risks: A note the director cannot re-explain the next day will be trusted less than the workbook, in a market where most CFOs already cannot explain an AI-made decision.
Once each site can ask for a daily cut, reporting hours rise, as they have in the finance teams that use these tools most.
A wrong site code or a late flex invoice in the nightly extract will be repeated in a clean sentence.
A cash line that pays a small supplier later than 30 days conflicts with BW 6:119a(6) if Noordhaven is a large company.
research_questions: How often does Monday's AFAS extract differ from the ledger the controller later signs, and on which accounts?
On a real month, how many minutes does the director need to explain every line of the note a day later?
Would the three site managers use one Monday page to place flex and overtime, or would they ask for a daily cut?
Is the forecast miss mostly volume and service, which finance does not own?

tasks.short: Set a shipper's credit limit and check the bank facility.

today.trigger: Sales asks for a limit on a new shipper or a raise, or Rabobank asks where the facility stands.
steps: Pull the shipper from AFAS: turnover, open items, days late and disputes.
Look up the KvK registration and whether the customer is a B.V. or a sole trader.
Read the sales mail and the contract terms on SharePoint.
Write the proposal and set the euro limit.
Tell sales, and have the limit recorded in AFAS.
drudgery: Retyping the same payment history and KvK facts into each proposal.
today.time_sinks: Thin files and sole traders take the longest, because the history is short and a wrong limit is easy to set.

lenses.faster: Gathering KvK, ledger history and the contract disappears, and that is most of each file. What stays is the decision on every request, about 15 minutes on a clear B.V. and longer on a sole trader, a bit under half the hours across the year.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when sales sends a limit request, when exposure crosses the review band, or on the facility review date. The fact sheet runs on its own. The gate is the director writing the euro limit before AFAS is changed.
lenses.ambitious: Sole-trader hauliers who today wait so long that they prepay get a limit decision within one working day. Demand would grow if the file were cheap, including in peak season, and the director still sets every euro amount.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping KvK extracts and payment history into a memo. The work worth keeping is the limit call on a shipper sales is pushing for.
lenses.options: A limit of €15,000, a limit of €40,000, or prepayment changes whether sales takes the first load. The fact sheet puts those three on the same exposure and pay history, and the director picks one.
lenses.altitude: Limit days become a run of short decisions on fact sheets, and file-building leaves the diary. The director keeps every euro decision, gains a standing duty to treat sole traders by hand, and becomes sharper on thin files and on shippers who matter commercially.
reach: The credit and collections officer's written limit file, once the director can read a dispute code and the payment term sales actually promised.

tasks.human_edge: The director sets the euro amount and stands behind a refusal to sales and to the shipper. A thin sole-trader file, a strategic shipper who pays late, and every customer who is a natural person stay with the director.
tasks.pattern_why: Each request has the same shape: KvK, AFAS history, the contract and current exposure. One call lays those facts out as a sheet the director can check. The euro limit is a decision, and for a sole trader a score would be the wrong output, so the call stops at the facts.

in_practice.trigger: Sales submits a limit request in the agreed mailbox, exposure crosses the review band, or the monthly Rabobank facility check falls due.
steps: The job collects KvK legal form, start date and directors, plus AFAS turnover, open items, disputes and the contract terms.
One model call writes a fact sheet: exposure, pay behaviour, legal form, and the gaps in the file.
The sheet states in the first line whether the customer is a natural person.
The director writes the euro limit, refuses the account, or requires prepayment.
On approval, the bookkeeper records that limit in AFAS and sales is told.
in_practice.human_gate: The director writes every limit before AFAS is updated. For a natural person the sheet carries facts and legal form, and the director sets the amount.
data_needed: Current exposure including orders not yet invoiced
in_practice.logs_to: The shipper dossier in AFAS and the SharePoint credit log: facts used, legal form, limit, approver and time.

evidence.claim: Scoring the creditworthiness of natural persons is high-risk under Annex III, point 5(b), of the EU AI Act.
Figures pasted into personal chatbots, and workpapers an auditor cannot rebuild, are a known failure in accounting teams. An approved tool with a log is the practical response.
At Noordhaven a loan application is a shipper credit limit or a review of the Rabobank facility. Sole-trader hauliers are natural persons.

risks: A fact sheet that ranks or scores a sole trader is high-risk under the EU AI Act, and a wrong refusal is hard to explain to that haulier.
Sales will push toward the top of any band that appears on the sheet, so the sheet carries facts and leaves the amount blank.
KvK data can be stale, and a new B.V. with no pay history looks clean in its first months.
A limit set in a personal chatbot leaves no file the accountant or the shipper can be shown.
research_questions: Of the last 50 limit requests, how many customers were B.V.s and how many were sole traders?
On those files, what share of the hours was gathering KvK and AFAS facts, as opposed to the decision itself?
Will sales treat the fact sheet as pressure to approve the highest recent limit for a similar shipper?
Do refusals today rest on credit-bureau data that would need its own licence and a stated legal basis?

tasks.short: See what is still unpaid and whether it will come in.

today.trigger: More than once a week the director looks at what is still unpaid, and again when cash is tight.
steps: Run the AFAS ageing and paste it into the collections workbook.
Compare it with the credit officer's notes and any promised dates.
Add up exposure on the largest shippers and by site.
Decide which balances are a real collection problem.
Tell the credit officer who to call, and whether a hold is allowed.
drudgery: Adding up buckets AFAS already stores, and rewriting the same overdue list.
today.time_sinks: The long tail of small balances, and disputes that are really complaints about a missed slot or damaged freight.

lenses.faster: Building and re-adding the ageing disappears. What stays is about half an hour a week on the flags, the holds and the payment plans, roughly three tenths of this task.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the morning job ages AFAS open items. The ageing, DSO and the six-week cash-in schedule run on their own. The gate is a hold, a payment plan or a write-off, which wait for the director.
lenses.ambitious: Once a week the credit officer works a six-week cash-in list, a forward decision Dutch finance teams rarely make: only 12% plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead. Demand from the management team and Rabobank would grow if the list were cheap, so it stays one list a week.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss adding up ageing buckets the ledger already stores. The work worth keeping is deciding what to do about a shipper who is late because a site missed the slot.
lenses.options: Calling, agreeing a plan, or stopping loads changes both the six-week cash-in and the relationship with that shipper. The list shows those options on the same balances, and the director chooses.
lenses.altitude: The full ageing leaves the week, which then holds the flags and the awkward shippers. The director keeps the right to hold freight, agree a plan or write off, and becomes more expert on disputes and on the cost of losing a shipper.
reach: The credit and collections officer's weekly call priority, once the director can see which late balances are service disputes at a named site.

tasks.human_edge: The director can tell a late balance caused by a missed slot or damaged freight from a shipper who will not pay, and can judge when stopping a load costs more than the debt. That call stays with the director.
tasks.pattern_why: Ageing, DSO and a cash-in schedule are rules on open items, due dates and promised dates. They can be coded and run each morning. A model is not required to add up balances.

in_practice.trigger: Each working morning after the AFAS open items are available. The director is called when a rule breaks.
steps: Open items are aged by shipper and by site, and DSO is calculated from the same file.
A six-week cash-in schedule uses due dates and promised dates where AFAS holds them.
Rules flag a broken promise, a dispute, a shipper over the exposure band, and any total that moves Rabobank covenant headroom.
The credit officer receives the call list. The director receives the flags.
The director decides any hold, payment plan or write-off, and the bookkeeper records it in AFAS.
in_practice.human_gate: A credit hold, a payment plan or a write-off waits for the director. The ageing is issued as a calculation from that morning's open items.
in_practice.logs_to: A weekly SharePoint snapshot that can be rebuilt from that morning's AFAS open items, plus the director's decision on each flag.

evidence.claim: Of 336 Dutch finance professionals, 81% explain DSO after the fact and only 12% plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead.
Data quality is the top barrier to finance use of AI, cited by 40.4% in the 2026 CFO survey. An ageing built on dirty dispute codes will be wrong with confidence.
Outstanding balances, ageing buckets and DSO at Noordhaven are arithmetic on AFAS open items for shippers of a logistics company.

risks: A hold on a dispute that is really a missed slot at Venlo loses the shipper and does not bring the cash in.
If promised dates live in the credit officer's notes, the six-week plan is due-date arithmetic and will miss the dates the team already knows.
A threshold set too low puts the whole tail back on the director's desk and the time saving goes.
research_questions: What share of overdue euro value is a service or damage dispute, measured on the last two quarters?
Are promised pay dates stored in AFAS on enough invoices to build a six-week cash-in?
When DSO has moved in the past year, did it move after holds and calls, or only after the mix of shippers changed?

tasks.short: Prepare the reports the board, the bank and the law require.

today.trigger: Month close, a board meeting, a Rabobank covenant date, or the annual accounts.
steps: Wait until the controller has closed the period in AFAS.
Take the trial balance into the board workbook and the covenant sheet.
Draft the points that need a decision, including provisions and trips still on the road.
Send the pack to the board and, at year end, to the external accountant.
Answer questions and sign.
drudgery: Rebuilding tables after late journals, and keeping two workbooks in step.
today.time_sinks: The days after close when the numbers still move, and the annual file the accountant rebuilds outside AFAS.

lenses.faster: Copying the trial balance into the board and covenant workbooks disappears. What stays is the reading, the judgments and the signature, about three fifths of these hours, with more of that in the annual close.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the controller marks the period ready, or ten working days before a board, bank or filing date. The tables fill from a stored mapping. The gate is the director's signature on that version.
lenses.ambitious: The works council receives, on the calendar already agreed with the OR, the financial note it is entitled to, drawn from the same pack as the board. Demand would stay on that calendar: a cheaper note would not create extra OR meetings.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting the trial balance into two workbooks after every late journal. The work worth keeping is the provision and the wording the director is willing to sign.
lenses.options: Booking a damage provision now, or waiting for the insurer's figure, changes the result the board sees and the covenant headroom. The pack shows both amounts tied to the ledger, and the director chooses which version is issued.
lenses.altitude: Close week becomes reading ties and writing a few judgments, then signing, and the workbook maintenance leaves the week. The director keeps the signature, gains a pack that shows broken ties before it is sent, and the expertise that grows is provisions, cut-off and what the OR should hear.
reach: The controller's tie-out of the board pack to the trial balance, once the director can read the mapping and the usual adjustment types. The SBR filing stays with the external accountant while AFAS cannot produce it for a large company.

tasks.human_edge: The director signs, and so owns the provision, the cut-off on trips still out, and what the OR is told about the company's position. The auditor will ask the director about those judgments.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack is a mapping from AFAS accounts to lines the board, Rabobank and the annual accounts already use. That mapping can be coded and checked. The judgments stay in the director's own words, because a generated paragraph is a weak file for the accountant.

in_practice.trigger: The controller marks the AFAS period ready, or a board date, covenant date or filing date is ten working days away.
steps: A mapping maintained by the controller ties ledger accounts to the board pack, the covenant ratios and the annual-account lines.
The job fills those tables and lists ties that fail, late journals, and provisions that are still a manual amount.
The director writes the decisions: the provision, the cut-off on open trips, and the OR note, in their own words.
The director signs that version. The board, Rabobank and the OR receive only the signed version.
The external accountant prepares the SBR filing where AFAS cannot do it.
in_practice.human_gate: The board, Rabobank, the OR and the external accountant receive only the version the director has signed.
data_needed: The account mapping and its version
Trips completed and not yet invoiced
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint statutory folder: mapping version, extract date, pack, signature, and the list of who received it.

evidence.claim: Large companies file accounts with the KVK via SBR from financial year 2025, and AFAS cannot produce that filing for them.
Tax estimates need mandatory human review and approval, with timestamped logs.

After the Omnibus changes, CSRD applies above 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover. Noordhaven's turnover is not in the company profile, so a CSRD report is out of scope until that figure is known.
The cabinet wants B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and digital reporting from 1 July 2031, with the bill before summer 2027. That is a dated project, separate from this month's board pack.

risks: If Noordhaven is a large company, a tidy board pack still leaves the SBR filing as a rebuild, because AFAS cannot produce it.
A wrong mapping sends the same error to the board, Rabobank and the OR.
Drifting back to a generated directors' report leaves a file the accountant cannot rebuild from the ledger.
An OR note with employee-level pay or absence would go beyond what finance should hold under the AVG.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven meet two of the three size tests for a large company, and who files the SBR accounts today?
How many hours does the external accountant spend rebuilding figures that already sit in AFAS?
What financial note has the OR already agreed to receive, and on which dates?
Is turnover above €450 million? Below that line, CSRD stays out of this task.

tasks.short: Review how finance works and what should change.

today.trigger: A close runs late, the auditor books an adjustment, a new agency portal arrives, or someone asks to change how invoices or cash are handled.
steps: Look at where the time went: manual journals, unmatched invoices, late agency hours and audit adjustments.
Talk to the controller, the bookkeepers and, if the work of staff would change, the OR.
Compare the procedure on SharePoint with what the three sites actually do.
Write a recommendation to change the procedure, the system or the budget for the work.
Decide what is worth doing this quarter.
drudgery: Collecting examples one by one from three sites and three agency invoice formats.
today.time_sinks: Understanding a workaround that only the night coordinator at one site can explain.

lenses.faster: Listing journals, match failures and late closes gets faster, and that is about a third of this task. The sessions with the controller, the bookkeepers and, where staff work would change, the OR stay, and they are the rest.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a close is late, the auditor adjusts a figure, or someone proposes a new way of working. A failure list can be prepared on its own. The gate is the director's recommendation, and the OR is informed first if staff work would change.
lenses.ambitious: Once a quarter the director and the controller decide which checks still earn their keep, a decision that today waits for the annual audit letter. Demand would grow if the review were cheap, because each site would bring its own workaround, so the review stays one a quarter.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss collecting screenshots of the same manual journal from three sites. The work worth keeping is deciding which check to drop and which failure is real.
lenses.options: Matching agency invoices inside AFAS, or keeping the spreadsheet a site already uses, changes where errors are caught and whether the OR must be consulted. The failure list puts both options on the same errors.
lenses.altitude: The quarter holds one working session on real failures, and a site visit when the list is odd, and the hunt for examples shrinks. The director gains the right to drop a check and to name which tool may read the ledger, and becomes more expert on where the process fails on a shift.
reach: The controller's list of control weaknesses, once the director has sat with a bookkeeper on an agency invoice that will not match.

tasks.human_edge: The director can tell a check that catches real errors from one that only slows a warehouse shift, and can tell when a change is large enough that the OR has to be in the room. The decision to let a tool read the ledger stays with the director.
tasks.pattern_why: What should change depends on the site, the auditor and sometimes the OR, so the director stays the lead. A prepared list of failures makes the session shorter. The recommendation itself is the director's work.

in_practice.trigger: A close misses the agreed day, the auditor books an adjustment, or a procedure change is proposed.
steps: A job lists the quarter's manual journals, unmatched agency invoices, late closes and audit points from AFAS.
The director and the controller read that list and check one real example at a site.
The director writes the recommendation: keep the check, change it, or drop it. A draft may be turned from their notes in the approved workspace.
If staff work would change, the OR is informed before the change is introduced.
The control log records which tools may read AFAS or the bank files, including the path toward e-invoicing on 1 July 2030.
in_practice.human_gate: The director signs the recommendation. A tool reads the ledger only after that approval is in the control log. The OR is informed before a change in staff work is introduced.
data_needed: The inventory of tools that can read AFAS or Rabobank files
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint control log: the evidence list, the recommendation, the decision, whether the OR was informed, and the approved tool list.

evidence.claim: 66% of CFOs describe central or comprehensive AI controls, against 45% of managers. Data quality is the top barrier, at 40.4%.
An advisor's control pattern for finance agents is timestamped logs, mandatory human approval on the judgments that move cash or tax, and a named governance lead in finance.
Giving people an approved tool, with a workpaper an auditor can rebuild, is the practical answer to shadow AI in accounting. Blocking personal chatbots on its own leaves the work with nowhere to go.
AFAS Profit sends and receives Peppol and is not Peppol-first. The cabinet's B2B e-invoicing date is 1 July 2030 and digital reporting is 1 July 2031.

risks: A tool connected to the ledger without a log fails the first question from the auditor.
CFOs describe stronger AI controls than managers see, so a SharePoint policy can leave the night shift on the old workaround.
Usage-based pricing has pushed AI spend over budget for 83% of finance executives in the Pigment survey, by about 27% on average.
A change in how invoices are matched can be a change in work the OR must hear about before it starts.
research_questions: Of the audit adjustments in the last two years, which came from the procedure and which from a judgment such as a provision?
Would the OR treat a change in invoice matching as a change in work it has to be told about?
Which tools already read AFAS or the Rabobank files outside an approved list?

tasks.short: Prepare the monthly risk and operations report.

today.trigger: The monthly management meeting, or a scare on fuel, a large debtor, overtime or a covenant.
steps: Pull site results, overtime, flex cost, damage and the debtor position.
Ask FP&A and the sites what sits behind any odd number.
Write the operational and risk report in PowerPoint or Excel.
Choose the few points the management team should act on.
drudgery: Refreshing the same charts and reformatting them for the pack.
today.time_sinks: Explaining a spike that was a wrong site code, then rewriting the page.

lenses.faster: Hand-updating the charts disappears, about half this task. What stays is about two to three hours a month to cut the page back to real risks and take it to the management team, and that holds while there is one page.
lenses.autonomous: It starts on the fifth working day. The single page fills on its own from AFAS. The gate is the director approving that page, and a further page only if the director asks for it.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift leads at the three warehouses receive the same short site strip the management team sees, covering damage, overtime and flex cost, a group that gets no such page today. Demand would grow if it were cheap, so the strip stays one page, three sites, once a month, with site totals only.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss refreshing the same charts for a pack that repeats last month. The work worth keeping is choosing the risk the management team will actually take up.
lenses.options: Naming fuel, a debtor or overtime as the risk on the one page changes what the management team spends the month on. The other breaches stay on a backup list the director can open.
lenses.altitude: The month holds one page and the management meeting, and the chart updates leave the diary. The director gains the right to keep the pack to that single page, keeps the choice of which risk is named, and becomes better at telling a coding error from a loss that will repeat.
reach: The FP&A analyst's site slide in the monthly pack, once the director can read overtime, flex and damage from the site totals.

tasks.human_edge: The director can tell a coding error or a late agency invoice from a loss that will repeat next month, and chooses the few risks the management team has time to act on. That choice stays with the director.
tasks.pattern_why: The page is the same measures every month, filled from AFAS and compared with thresholds. That is code. A model writing extra commentary would add pages the management team did not ask for.

in_practice.trigger: The fifth working day of the month, for one operations and risk page.
steps: The job fills a fixed page: result by site, overtime, flex cost against plan, damage, debtor flags, fuel against budget, and covenant headroom.
Lines that move past the threshold are listed with the AFAS account and the extract date.
The director strikes out noise, such as a wrong site code or a flex invoice in the wrong period, and keeps the risks that need a decision.
The approved page goes to the management team.
A site strip can go to the night-shift leads, built from site totals, with no employee names and no individual wages.
in_practice.human_gate: The management team receives the page only after the director approves it. A second pack, or a pack for one site, waits for the director to ask for it.
data_needed: Overtime and flex cost at site level
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint risk-pack folder: the month, the thresholds, the page, the lines struck out, and who received it.

evidence.claim: The finance teams furthest along with AI are more likely to spend over 40 hours a month on executive reporting (30%, against 17% of early-stage teams). A risk pack that is easy to copy will multiply.
Workpapers an auditor cannot rebuild are a documented shadow-AI failure in accounting. The page has to be reproducible from the AFAS extract.
At Noordhaven the operational risks in this report are site result, own labour, flex, fuel, damage, debtors and the Rabobank covenant, across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

risks: One easy page becomes a page per site and per shift, and the month then takes more reporting time than the workbook did.
Site totals for a small night team can still identify people. The strip has to stay coarse enough for the AVG.
A threshold set too tight trains the management team to ignore the page.
research_questions: Which lines on the risk page in the last four quarters led to a decision, and which were restated the next month as coding errors?
Will the management team accept one page a month once the first page is easy to produce?
Can the night-shift strip be filled from site totals alone, with no names and no individual wages?

tasks.short: Build the cost budget with the sites.

today.trigger: The budget round, or a cost miss that means the year plan is no longer one the business can be held to.
steps: Collect AFAS actuals by site for labour, flex, fuel, housing and damage.
Get flex hours and rates from the three agency portals, and the CAO rises from HR.
Build the cost bridge in Excel with the FP&A analysts.
Walk through it with the site managers and the HR Director.
Set the budget the management team will be held to.
drudgery: Cleaning agency spreadsheets so the hours match the invoices in AFAS.
today.time_sinks: Labour, because own staff under the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO, and 150 to 300 flex workers, do not sit in one report.

lenses.faster: Cleaning agency files and assembling the first bridge gets shorter, about a third of this task. The sessions with the site managers and HR, and the final budget choice, stay.
lenses.autonomous: It starts on the budget calendar, and again before peak season when flex is about to be ordered. The cost cube can be built on its own. The gate is the director setting the budget after the sessions with the sites and HR.
lenses.ambitious: Before peak season the HR Director and the three site managers get a labour decision on own hours versus flex inside the 150 to 300 range, in time to place the agency order. Demand would grow in the months before peak, and again if each site could request its own rerun, so the round stays two scenarios and three sites.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss cleaning three agency spreadsheets so they match AFAS. The work worth keeping is the labour choice with the site managers and HR, inside the CAO.
lenses.options: A budget with more own drivers, and a budget with flex at the top of the seasonal range, change hiring, the agency order and the conversation with the OR. Both use the same CAO rates and the same agency rates.
lenses.altitude: Budget time moves into the sessions with the three sites and HR, with the cube ready before the room. The director keeps the final number, gains two scenarios that force the flex-versus-own choice into the open, and becomes more expert on the CAO build-up and the peak-season range.
reach: The FP&A analyst's labour-cost bridge, once the director can follow a CAO rate and an agency invoice back to hours. Payroll calculation and named absence files stay with the payroll specialist and HR.

tasks.human_edge: The director judges the labour cost the sites and the OR will actually work to, including the mix across the transport CAO, the warehouse CAO and the flex range. That choice is made in the room, with HR and the site managers.
tasks.pattern_why: The cost cube is a repeatable pull from AFAS and the agency portals. The budget itself is a choice with the site managers, HR and the CAO, so the director stays the lead and works from a draft.

in_practice.trigger: The budget calendar, and a pre-peak session with HR when the seasonal flex order is about to be placed.
steps: A cube is built from AFAS and the three agency portals: own labour, flex, fuel and housing, by site.
Illness cost enters as a site total from payroll. Named absence files stay with HR, including the Wet verbetering poortwachter file.
FP&A checks the cube against the invoices, and HR confirms the CAO rates and the agency rates.
Two scenarios are walked with the site managers and the HR Director: more own hours, or flex inside the 150 to 300 range.
The director sets the budget the management team will be held to.
in_practice.human_gate: The director sets the budget after the site and HR sessions. The cube is the input to that meeting.
data_needed: Actuals by site and cost type
CAO rate card for transport and for the warehouse
Illness cost as a site total
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder: cube version, the two scenarios, the choice, and who was in the room.

evidence.claim: Data quality is the barrier most often named by finance executives (40.4%). Agency hours that do not match AFAS invoices will make both budget scenarios look exact and both be wrong.

At Noordhaven own warehouse and transport staff fall under the transport CAO and the company's warehouse CAO, and flex runs from about 150 to 300 people through three agencies. Illness cost is a payroll total; the Wet verbetering poortwachter case stays with HR.

risks: Agency hours that do not match the AFAS invoices make both scenarios wrong while looking finished.
Pulling named illness records into the cube would breach the AVG and would cut across the Wet verbetering poortwachter work HR already does.
A cheap rerun for every site multiplies budget versions the management team has not agreed.
research_questions: Where did last year's budget miss land: volume, own labour, flex, fuel, or housing?
Do the three agency portals show hours by site and week, or only a monthly invoice total?
On the last peak, would a second labour scenario have changed the flex order, or was the order already fixed by customer contracts?

tasks.short: Check fuel, interest and currency against the budget.

today.trigger: A fuel invoice looks high, the Rabobank facility is due to roll, or someone asks whether a lane's currency has moved.
steps: Check diesel and AdBlue prices against the rate in the budget.
Check the facility interest basis and any foreign-currency exposure on live lanes.
See whether the surcharge clauses filed on SharePoint have been reached.
Tell sales and FP&A whether the budget rate or the surcharge should change.
drudgery: Collecting prices from invoices and mail into one sheet.
today.time_sinks: Finding which contracts allow a surcharge, and which diesel rate was assumed in the budget.

lenses.faster: Collecting diesel, interest and currency quotes disappears, about three fifths of this task. What stays is the breach decision, a short meeting with sales in the weeks the band breaks, and no review in the other weeks.
lenses.autonomous: It starts each week when prices are loaded, and the director hears only when diesel, the facility rate or a currency breaks the budget band. The comparison runs on its own. The gate is a surcharge change, a budget-rate change, or a fix on the facility.
lenses.ambitious: In the week diesel crosses the standard surcharge clause, sales is told the company rate to apply, a decision that today waits for a quarterly look. Demand would grow when diesel is volatile, and again if every lane wanted its own rate, so the watch uses one company clause and fires on a breach.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss collecting diesel and rate quotes into a sheet. The work worth keeping is the decision to change a surcharge or to absorb the move.
lenses.options: Passing the diesel move through the surcharge, absorbing it in the margin, or fixing more of the facility changes what sales may promise a shipper. The exception states the euro effect of each on current volume, and the director picks one.
lenses.altitude: Weeks inside the band need nothing from the director. A breach week is one decision with sales. The director keeps the surcharge and facility decision, gains the euro effect before that conversation, and becomes more expert on the clause and on the promise already made to a shipper.
reach: The FP&A analyst's fuel-rate update, once the director knows which shipper contracts share the standard surcharge clause.

tasks.human_edge: The director knows what sales has already promised a shipper, and judges whether this is the week to change a surcharge or to take the diesel move in the margin. A price feed cannot make or break that promise. A fix on the facility stays a director's decision, and the board's where the board has reserved it.
tasks.pattern_why: A price against a budget rate, a margin effect on current volume, and a clause threshold are arithmetic and can run every week. The surcharge decision and any fix on the facility stay with the director, with a log.

in_practice.trigger: Each week when fuel prices, the Rabobank interest basis and the currencies on live lanes are loaded. The director is called when a band breaks.
steps: Diesel, AdBlue, the facility interest basis and the currencies on live lanes are compared with the budget rates.
The job computes the margin effect on current volume by site.
It checks the standard surcharge clause held on SharePoint and states whether the clause has been reached.
A breach opens one exception with three options: change the surcharge, change the budget rate, or absorb the move.
The director decides, sales is told, and a facility fix waits for the director and, where reserved, for the board.
in_practice.human_gate: Sales is told of a surcharge or a budget-rate change only after the director decides. A facility fix or a bulk fuel commitment waits for that decision and a log entry.
data_needed: Budget rates for diesel, interest and currency
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint market log: the prices, the variance, the euro effect, the decision, and the date sales was told.

evidence.claim: Strategic purchases and cash allocation need mandatory human review and approval, with timestamped logs.
At Noordhaven the price review behind this task is diesel and AdBlue, the Rabobank interest basis, and currency on live lanes, read against the budget and the shipper surcharge clause.

risks: Applying a company-wide surcharge to a contract that fixes the rate for a year is a commercial breach.
Treating the alert as an order, and fixing the facility or buying fuel forward without the director's log, skips the approval those commitments need.
Fuel-card spend coded to the wrong site moves the apparent margin between Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
research_questions: Do the largest shipper contracts share one surcharge clause, or does each major customer have its own?
Is the diesel price already on the fuel invoices in AFAS, and how many days late is it?
Who is allowed to change a surcharge today: the director, sales, or the board?
Would a surcharge in the week the clause breaks conflict with annual rates already signed?

role.altitude: The week moves from assembling packs in Excel to a short list of judgments: the forecast the management team will be held to, the shipper limits, the provisions, the surcharge, and which finance check still earns its place. The director gains the right to set the thresholds and the list of tools that may read AFAS or the bank files, and keeps the signature on the forecast, the limit and the filing. The expertise that grows is the three sites, the shippers and an audit trail someone else can rebuild.
reach: The FP&A analysts' Monday variance note and fuel-rate bridge, once the director can trace volume, flex hours and diesel to a site result.
The credit and collections officer's call priority and written limit file, once the director can read a dispute and the term sales promised. The calls to shippers stay with that officer.

The controller's tie-out of the board pack to the trial balance, once the director can read the mapping. The SBR filing remains the external accountant's work while AFAS cannot produce it for a large company.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 690 hours a year, 43% of the role. The rest is the team of 10, the Rabobank relationship, the shippers and the board in person, and a faster pack does not shrink that. One director cannot read a pack per site per day, and reporting hours rise when packs multiply. Scoring sole traders for credit is high-risk under the EU AI Act. If the company is large for filing purposes, AFAS still cannot file the SBR accounts. The Power BI extract is a night behind the ledger, and a forecast the business trusts still depends on the volume figures operations provides.
skills_to_grow: Read an AFAS reconciliation and a CAMT.053 well enough to catch a wrong site or a missing agency invoice.
Set exception thresholds and keep a log an external auditor can rebuild from the source file.
Apply the EU AI Act line between a fact sheet and a credit score where the shipper is a sole trader.
Follow a CAO wage and an agency rate back to hours at site level, and leave named absence files with HR.
Read the standard fuel-surcharge clause and the Rabobank facility so a price move becomes a euro decision.
Know which figures the OR already receives, and keep them at company or site level.
role.ambitious_version: Aimed higher, this director would hold a 13-week cash and margin view that Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo use before they order flex or overtime, a credit decision on a logged fact sheet within one working day, and a weekly collection list aimed at the cash expected in the next six weeks. The board, Rabobank and the OR would take their figures from one pack that ties to AFAS, on a close that lands inside the days already agreed. The director's own time would sit on the forecast they will defend, the limits, the provisions, the surcharge and the few control changes that survive a quarter.
